headline: Nick Suzuki's Injury Emphasizes Montreal Canadiens' Need For Center Depth
take:
The Hockey News reports that Nick Suzuki's ironman streak is ending at 546 games, which it says reinforces the Montreal Canadiens' need to pursue an upgrade at center.

The numbers show why his absence matters. So far this season, Suzuki has 12 points in 9 games and 21.78 minutes a night, and MTL has controlled 57 percent of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he's on the ice at five-on-five. The team is 7-3-2, but its overall expected goal share is 48.8 percent, and it has leaned on goalie play, with 5.5 goals saved above expected. A team in that spot can't easily afford to lose its top center. In the 3 games since he went out, Oliver Kapanen has moved up beside Slafkovský and Caufield, going to 15:06 a night from 11:05, and Jake Evans is up to 16:54 from 13:02. That's based on games already played without him, and it's the pairing to watch for fantasy value.
